text:
maya: Heads up — after the gpu-operator rollout to eu-west-1 at ~07:00 UTC a bunch of inference pods failed to get GPUs. Seeing allocation errors and some CrashLoopBackOffs.

jon: I see a spike in scheduling failures in prometheus: -> kube_scheduler_scheduler_attempts? We lost ~40% of listed GPU capacity in that region. Autoscaler tried to add nodes but pods remained unschedulable.

li: kubectl describe on one affected node shows the device plugin advertising 0 GPUs: 

```
Name: gpu-plugin-nvidia-xxxxx
Status: Ready
AllocatedResources: nvidia.com/gpu=0
Events: PodReady: False - plugin failed to initialize: driver mismatch: kernel module built for 520.14, user driver 520.56
```

taylor: What did the operator change in the rollout? I noticed gpu-operator image bumped to 1.12.0 and device-plugin to v0.13.0. That release added a stricter cuda_version check in its preflight / registration path. If the node driver/kernel combo doesn’t match, kubelet rejects the device plugin.

maya: Confirmed. The operator's new admission hooks now validate driver vs cuda versions and mark the plugin as not-ready instead of fibbing that GPUs are present. Good for correctness but brutal in practice when driver module compilation lags.

li: Quick diagnostics we ran: 
- ssh node -> sudo modinfo nvidia | grep -i version -> shows 520.56
- nvidia-smi -> errors: "NVIDIA-SMI has failed because it couldn't communicate with the NVIDIA driver"
- dmesg shows "nvidia: disagrees about version of symbol module_layout" -> classic kernel module mismatch after kernel upgrade.

jon: Looks like two contributing vectors: (1) kernel upgrade on some nodes left DKMS modules not rebuilt, (2) operator/device-plugin version now enforces cuda/driver checks. Combined -> plugin refuses to advertise GPUs -> scheduler can't place pods.

taylor: Temporary mitigation applied: cordoned affected nodes, rolled operator image back to 1.11.3 in eu-west-1 (helm rollback) so device-plugin becomes permissive again. Then we drained a few nodes and reinstalled the NV driver package to match kernel (nvidia-driver 520.56 with DKMS rebuild).

maya: Commands used for driver re-install (for reference):
```bash
sudo apt-get install --reinstall nvidia-driver-520=520.56-0ubuntu0
sudo dkms autoinstall
sudo systemctl restart kubelet
```
then check: `nvidia-smi` -> should show GPUs.

li: After pushing fixes to ~8 nodes, gpu capacity returned and pending pods started scheduling. We also cleared stale device-plugin pods so the new plugin could re-register.

deploy-bot: Deploy event: gpu-operator:1.12.0 -> rolled back to gpu-operator:1.11.3 in namespace gpu-operator by maya at 2025-04-12T07:42:00Z 

jon: Impact note: ~2 hours of reduced capacity in eu-west-1, ~120 inference task failures (retries handled most), Dedicated customers on reserved pools saw degraded throughput. Need a postmortem and customer comms draft.

maya: Agreed. Immediate actions:
- Pin gpu-operator in kustomize for all regions to 1.11.3 until we validate upgrade testing.
- Add cluster preflight to rollout pipeline to run quick `nvidia-smi` + kernel module check on a canary node before operator rollout.
- Add automated DKMS rebuild job after kernel upgrades (or block kernel upgrades until driver test passes).
- Add sales/CS blurb summarizing impact and mitigation.

taylor: Long term: update our node image CI to test kernel + driver combos used in production; add a compatibility matrix in infra docs. Also maybe tweak operator config to allow a grace period where device-plugin advertises GPUs but marks them tainted? (we discussed that earlier)

li: Note re NCCL: some pods that did schedule but had mismatched driver versions exhibited silent instability in multi-GPU allreduce. We'll run targeted NCCL tests during the node validation window.

maya: I'll own the postmortem. Putting a runbook together now with the steps we used. If anyone has command snippets or logs to add, paste here.

jon: +1, dropping the kubelet/systemd logs from one node: `journalctl -u kubelet -n 200` shows device-plugin restarts and then "failed to list devices: driver not loaded" errors. Adding to the runbook.

maya: Thanks all. We'll follow up with a short customer note and schedule an operator upgrade playbook review. :thumbsup:
